title: Bregman distances and variational source rates

items.title: Banach-space convex subgradients and dual pairings

references.title: Barbara Kaltenbacher, Convergence rates under a range invariance condition with application to electrical impedance tomography, §1, notation and convex analysis tools
Jonathan M. Borwein and Jon D. Vanderwerff, Convex Functions: Constructions, Characterizations and Counterexamples, §§4.1 and 4.4

items.statement:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space and let $X^*$ be its continuous real dual. The dual pairing is evaluation, written $\langle \xi,x\rangle_{X^*,X}:=\xi(x)$ for $\xi\in X^*$ and $x\in X$. Let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be a proper convex functional: $R$ never takes the value $-\infty$, its effective domain $\operatorname{dom}R:=\{x\in X:R(x)<+\infty\}$ is nonempty, and $R((1-t)x+tz)\le (1-t)R(x)+tR(z)$ for $x,z\in X$ and $t\in[0,1]$, with $0\cdot(+\infty):=0$ for this convex-combination formula. For $x\in\operatorname{dom}R$, its subdifferential is

$$\partial R(x):=\{\xi\in X^*:R(z)\ge R(x)+\langle\xi,z-x\rangle_{X^*,X}\text{ for every }z\in X\}.$$

An element of $\partial R(x)$ is a subgradient of $R$ at $x$. Set $\partial R(x):=\varnothing$ when $x\notin\operatorname{dom}R$. The subdifferential may be empty at a point of $\operatorname{dom}R$; no nonemptiness assertion is part of this definition.

items.title: A conjugate bound for residual and Bregman errors

references.title: Barbara Kaltenbacher, Convergence rates under a range invariance condition with application to electrical impedance tomography, Lemma 2
Frederic Weidling, Variational Source Conditions and Conditional Stability Estimates for Inverse Problems in PDEs, Theorem 2.20

items.statement:
Let $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous, nondecreasing, concave, and satisfy $\psi(0)=0$. Extend $g=-\psi$ to $\mathbb R$ by $g(s)=+\infty$ for $s<0$, and define $H(q):=g^*(-q)=\sup_{s\ge0}(\psi(s)-qs)$ for $q>0$, assuming the displayed suprema below are finite. For $c_1,c_2,C_3,\alpha>0$ and $d,r,e\ge0$, if

$$c_1r+c_2\alpha e\le d+\alpha\psi(C_3r),$$

then

$$e\le\frac1{c_2}\left(\frac d\alpha+H\!\left(\frac{c_1}{C_3\alpha}\right)\right),\qquad r\le\frac2{c_1}\left(d+\alpha H\!\left(\frac{c_1}{2C_3\alpha}\right)\right).$$

items.title: Fenchel–Young equality for a Banach regularizer

references.title: Jonathan M. Borwein and Jon D. Vanderwerff, Convex Functions: Constructions, Characterizations and Counterexamples, Proposition 4.4.1(a)

items.statement:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space, let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex, and define its Fenchel conjugate $R^*:X^*\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ by $R^*(\xi):=\sup_{z\in X}(\langle\xi,z\rangle_{X^*,X}-R(z))$. For every $x\in\operatorname{dom}R$ and $\xi\in X^*$, the Fenchel–Young inequality and its equality characterization are

$$R(x)+R^*(\xi)\ge\langle\xi,x\rangle_{X^*,X},\qquad R(x)+R^*(\xi)=\langle\xi,x\rangle_{X^*,X}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \xi\in\partial R(x).$$

items.title: Bregman distances for convex regularizers

references.title: Barbara Kaltenbacher, Convergence rates under a range invariance condition with application to electrical impedance tomography, equation (1.25)
Frederic Weidling, Variational Source Conditions and Conditional Stability Estimates for Inverse Problems in PDEs, Chapter 2

items.statement:
Let $X$ be a real Banach space, let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex, choose $x^\dagger\in\operatorname{dom}R$, and choose $\xi^\dagger\in\partial R(x^\dagger)$. For $x\in\operatorname{dom}R$, the **Bregman distance** generated by $\xi^\dagger$ from the reference point $x^\dagger$ to $x$ is

$$D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger):=R(x)-R(x^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,x-x^\dagger\rangle_{X^*,X}.$$

The subgradient inequality makes this quantity nonnegative, and $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x^\dagger,x^\dagger)=0$. The definition fixes the orientation: the first argument is the comparison point and the second is the reference point carrying the chosen subgradient.

items.title: Variational source conditions on a regularizer sublevel

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, equation (10.17)
Frederic Weidling, Variational Source Conditions and Conditional Stability Estimates for Inverse Problems in PDEs, equations (2.22) and (2.26)
Barbara Kaltenbacher, Convergence rates under a range invariance condition with application to electrical impedance tomography, equations (1.28)–(1.31)

items.statement:
Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, let $F:D(F)\subseteq X\to Y$, let $x^\dagger\in D(F)$ with exact datum $y=F(x^\dagger)$, and let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex with $x^\dagger\in\operatorname{dom}R$. Fix $\xi^\dagger\in\partial R(x^\dagger)$, an exponent $1\le p<\infty$, a continuous nondecreasing concave function $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ with $\psi(0)=0$ and $\psi(t)>0$ for $t>0$, a coefficient $0\le\beta<1$, and a level $R_0\ge R(x^\dagger)$. The **variational source condition** with these data holds on the named regularizer sublevel $L_{R_0}:=\{x\in D(F):R(x)\le R_0\}$ when

$$-\langle\xi^\dagger,x-x^\dagger\rangle_{X^*,X}\le\beta D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger)+\psi\!\left(\|F(x)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^p\right)\qquad(x\in L_{R_0}).$$

The condition is an assumption on the selected subgradient and the stated sublevel; it makes no assertion that a subgradient exists at every point or that a regularized minimizer exists.

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, Theorem 10.7

items.statement:
Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $D(F)\subseteq X$, and $F:D(F)\to Y$. Let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex, let $x^\dagger\in D(F)\cap\operatorname{dom}R$, set $y=F(x^\dagger)$, and choose $\xi^\dagger\in\partial R(x^\dagger)$. Fix $1\le p<\infty$, $0\le\beta<1$, and a level $R_0>R(x^\dagger)$. Let $\psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous, nondecreasing and concave, with $\psi(0)=0$ and $\psi(t)>0$ for $t>0$, and assume the variational source inequality

$$-\langle\xi^\dagger,x-x^\dagger\rangle_{X^*,X}\le\beta D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger)+\psi\!\left(\|F(x)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^p\right)\qquad\left(x\in L_{R_0}:=\{x\in D(F):R(x)\le R_0\}\right),$$

where $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger):=R(x)-R(x^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,x-x^\dagger\rangle_{X^*,X}$. Extend $-\psi$ by $+\infty$ on negative arguments and write $H(q):=(-\psi)^*(-q)=\sup_{s\ge0}(\psi(s)-qs)$; assume $H(q)$ is finite for sufficiently large $q$ and $H(q)\to0$ as $q\to\infty$. For sufficiently small noise levels $\delta>0$ and data $y^\delta\in Y$ with $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$, define $J_\alpha^\delta(x):=p^{-1}\|F(x)-y^\delta\|_Y^p+\alpha R(x)$. Suppose $\alpha=\alpha(\delta)>0$ tends to zero, $0\le\varepsilon_\delta\le C_\varepsilon\delta^p$, and $x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon}\in D(F)$ is an $\varepsilon_\delta$-minimizer, meaning $J_\alpha^\delta(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon})\le\inf_{z\in D(F)}J_\alpha^\delta(z)+\varepsilon_\delta$. Set $c_p:=2^{1-p}/p$ and $\rho_\delta:=H(c_p/\alpha(\delta))$. Assume that for constants $c_-,c_+,C_H>0$ independent of $\delta$,

$$c_-\delta^p\le\alpha(\delta)\rho_\delta\le c_+\delta^p,\qquad H(c_p/(2\alpha(\delta)))\le C_H\rho_\delta$$

for all sufficiently small $\delta$. Then for all sufficiently small $\delta$, $x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon}\in L_{R_0}$ and

$$D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon},x^\dagger)=O(\rho_\delta),\qquad \|F(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon})-y^\delta\|_Y=O(\delta).$$

If, in addition, $\psi(C_0\delta^p)=O(\rho_\delta)$ for a fixed $C_0$ such that $T_\delta:=\|F(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon})-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^p\le C_0\delta^p$ for all sufficiently small $\delta$, then $|R(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon})-R(x^\dagger)|=O(\rho_\delta)$. If also $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger)\ge c_R\|x-x^\dagger\|_X^s$ on $L_{R_0}$ for constants $c_R,s>0$, then $\|x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon}-x^\dagger\|_X^s=O(\rho_\delta)$.

In the Hilbert special case, set $p=2$ and suppose $X,Y$ are real Hilbert spaces, $F:U\to Y$ has the real open-domain interface of a nonlinear forward map, $x^\dagger$ is an $x_0$-minimum-norm exact solution, $R(x)=\frac12\|x-x_0\|_X^2$, and the source inequality on a regularizer sublevel contained in $U$ is

$$\langle x^\dagger-x_0,x^\dagger-x\rangle_X\le\beta_1\frac12\|x-x^\dagger\|_X^2+\beta_2\|F(x)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y$$

with $0\le\beta_1<1$ and $\beta_2\ge0$. For exact global minimizers of the nonlinear Tikhonov functional with $\alpha(\delta)\asymp\delta$, the theorem gives $\|x_{\alpha(\delta)}^\delta-x^\dagger\|_X=O(\sqrt\delta)$ and $\|F(x_{\alpha(\delta)}^\delta)-y^\delta\|_Y=O(\delta)$. The assertion is conditional on such a global minimizer being supplied; it does not assert existence or cover local numerical minima.

title: Bregman distances and variational source rates — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A unit VSC coefficient need not force Bregman convergence

references.title: Frederic Weidling, Variational Source Conditions and Conditional Stability Estimates for Inverse Problems in PDEs, Theorem 2.20 and equation (2.26)

items.statement:
For $X=Y=\mathbb R$ with the usual norm and pairing, $D(F)=\mathbb R$, $F(x)=0$, $R(x)=\max\{0,-x\}$, $x^\dagger=0$, $y=0$, $\xi^\dagger=-1\in\partial R(0)$, $R_0=1$, $p=2$, and $\psi(t)=\sqrt t$, the boundary source inequality with coefficient $\beta_1=1$

$$-\xi^\dagger(x-x^\dagger)\le D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger)+\psi\!\left(|F(x)-F(x^\dagger)|^2\right)\qquad(R(x)\le R_0),$$

holds for every $x$ with $R(x)\le R_0$, where $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,0):=R(x)-R(0)-\xi^\dagger x$. For every $\delta\in(0,1]$, set $y^\delta=0$, $\alpha(\delta)=\delta$, and $J_\delta(x):=\frac12|F(x)-y^\delta|^2+\alpha(\delta)R(x)$. A global minimizer means a point $x_\delta$ with $J_\delta(x_\delta)\le J_\delta(z)$ for every $z\in\mathbb R$. The false claim is that every family of such global minimizers satisfies $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x_\delta,0)=O(\delta)$ as $\delta\downarrow0$, meaning $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x_\delta,0)\le C\delta$ for some fixed $C$ and all sufficiently small $\delta>0$.

items.title: Power index functions give polynomial Bregman rates

references.title: Frederic Weidling, Variational Source Conditions and Conditional Stability Estimates for Inverse Problems in PDEs, equation (2.25a)
Barbara Kaltenbacher, Convergence rates under a range invariance condition with application to electrical impedance tomography, equation (1.32a)

items.statement:
Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $D(F)\subseteq X$, $F:D(F)\to Y$, and let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex. Fix $x^\dagger\in D(F)\cap\operatorname{dom}R$, $y=F(x^\dagger)$, $\xi^\dagger\in\partial R(x^\dagger)$, $1\le p<\infty$, $A>0$, $0<\mu<1$, $0\le\beta<1$, and $R_0>R(x^\dagger)$. Write $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger):=R(x)-R(x^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,x-x^\dagger\rangle_{X^*,X}$, and suppose

$$-\langle\xi^\dagger,x-x^\dagger\rangle_{X^*,X}\le\beta D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger)+A\|F(x)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^{p\mu}\qquad(x\in D(F),\ R(x)\le R_0).$$

For data $y^\delta$ with $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$, suppose $0\le\varepsilon_\delta\le C_\varepsilon\delta^p$ and $x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon}\in D(F)$ satisfies $J_\alpha^\delta(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon})\le\inf_{z\in D(F)}J_\alpha^\delta(z)+\varepsilon_\delta$, where $J_\alpha^\delta(x):=p^{-1}\|F(x)-y^\delta\|_Y^p+\alpha R(x)$. Set $c_p=2^{1-p}/p$, $H(q):=\sup_{s\ge0}(As^\mu-qs)$, and choose $\alpha(\delta)\asymp\delta^{p(1-\mu)}$. Then $H(c_p/\alpha)\asymp\delta^{p\mu}$ and $\alpha H(c_p/\alpha)\asymp\delta^p$. The fixed-scale conjugate and penalty-index conditions hold. Hence $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon},x^\dagger)=O(\delta^{p\mu})$ and $\|F(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon})-y^\delta\|_Y=O(\delta)$; if $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger)\ge c_R\|x-x^\dagger\|_X^s$ on $L_{R_0}$ for constants $c_R,s>0$, then $\|x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon}-x^\dagger\|_X=O(\delta^{p\mu/s})$.

items.title: Logarithmic index functions give log-rate Bregman convergence

references.title: Frederic Weidling, Variational Source Conditions and Conditional Stability Estimates for Inverse Problems in PDEs, equation (2.25b)
Barbara Kaltenbacher, Convergence rates under a range invariance condition with application to electrical impedance tomography, equations (1.31)–(1.32b)

items.statement:
Let $X,Y$ be real Banach spaces, $D(F)\subseteq X$, $F:D(F)\to Y$, and let $R:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]$ be proper and convex. Choose $x^\dagger\in D(F)\cap\operatorname{dom}R$, set $y=F(x^\dagger)$, and choose $\xi^\dagger\in\partial R(x^\dagger)$. Fix $1\le p<\infty$, $\nu>0$, $0<t_0<e^{-(\nu+1)}$, $0\le\beta<1$, and $R_0>R(x^\dagger)$. Define $\psi(0)=0$, $\psi(t)=(-\log t)^{-\nu}$ for $0<t<t_0$, and $\psi(t)=(-\log t_0)^{-\nu}$ for $t\ge t_0$. Suppose

$$-\langle\xi^\dagger,x-x^\dagger\rangle_{X^*,X}\le\beta D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger)+\psi\!\left(\|F(x)-F(x^\dagger)\|_Y^p\right)\qquad\left(x\in L_{R_0}:=\{x\in D(F):R(x)\le R_0\}\right),$$

where $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger):=R(x)-R(x^\dagger)-\langle\xi^\dagger,x-x^\dagger\rangle_{X^*,X}$. For data $y^\delta\in Y$ with $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$, let $0\le\varepsilon_\delta\le C_\varepsilon\delta^p$ and suppose $x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon}\in D(F)$ satisfies

$$J_\alpha^\delta(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon})\le\inf_{z\in D(F)}J_\alpha^\delta(z)+\varepsilon_\delta,\qquad J_\alpha^\delta(x):=p^{-1}\|F(x)-y^\delta\|_Y^p+\alpha R(x).$$

Choose $\alpha(\delta)=\delta^p(\log(1/\delta))^\nu$ for sufficiently small $0<\delta<1$, and write $c_p=2^{1-p}/p$. For $H(q):=\sup_{s\ge0}(\psi(s)-qs)$, one has $H(q)\sim(\log q)^{-\nu}$ as $q\to\infty$, so $\rho_\delta:=H(c_p/\alpha(\delta))\asymp(\log(1/\delta))^{-\nu}$ and $\alpha(\delta)\rho_\delta\asymp\delta^p$. The variational source rate theorem therefore gives

$$D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon},x^\dagger)=O((\log(1/\delta))^{-\nu}),\qquad \|F(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon})-y^\delta\|_Y=O(\delta),\qquad |R(x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon})-R(x^\dagger)|=O((\log(1/\delta))^{-\nu}).$$

If also $D_R^{\xi^\dagger}(x,x^\dagger)\ge c_R\|x-x^\dagger\|_X^s$ on $L_{R_0}$ for constants $c_R,s>0$, then $\|x_\alpha^{\delta,\varepsilon}-x^\dagger\|_X=O((\log(1/\delta))^{-\nu/s})$. The parameter coupling here is derived from $\alpha H(c_p/\alpha)\asymp\delta^p$.
